 HOOPS CENTRAL: Wofford vs. #8/9 Tennessee
 November 02, 2026 | Men's Basketball
 Tennessee Notes Wofford Notes Watch Live (SECN) Listen Live Live Stats Share: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. – The Tennessee men's basketball team is set to officially open the 2026-27 season Tuesday as it hosts the Wofford Terriers. Tipoff is set for 6 p.m. ET. 
 GAMEDAY TIMES & BROADCAST INFO
 Opponent:  Wofford Terriers 
 Tipoff:  Tuesday, Nov. 3 | 6 p.m. ET
 Venue:   Food City Center 
 Watch Online:  SECN 
 Online:   Listen Live |  Live Stats 
 RELATED LINKS
  Gameday Information   Follow @Vol_Hoops   
 TENNESSEE
 Roster Schedule   Game Notes 
 WOFFORD
 Roster Schedule   Game Notes 
 THE LATEST FROM THE VOLS
 Harris Selected to Naismith Trophy Watch List Vols Sold Out of Season Tickets for Fourth Year in a Row Harris Among 20 on NABC Player of the Year Preseason Watch List Harris Tabbed Preseason Second Team All-SEC by Coaches Harris on Julius Erving Award Top 20 Preseason Watch List 
Fans can watch Tuesday's game on SEC Network and stream the game on Watch ESPN.com and the ESPN app. Roy Philpott (play-by-play) and Richard Hendrix (color) will have the call.
Fans state-wide can tune in to their local Vol Network radio affiliate to hear Voice of the Vols Mike Keith and analyst Chris Lofton depict the action.
Tennessee is coming off an exceptional 2025-26 campaign which included 25 victories, a fourth-straight appearance in the Sweet 16 and a third-straight trip to the Elite Eight. 
 THE MATCHUP 
• After playing three times in 365 days from 12/2/52 to 12/1/53, the sides met four times in the next 69 seasons (1954-2023), but are now doing so for the third time in the last four campaigns (2023-27).
• The last matchup was an NCAA Round of 64 affair in Lexington, Ky., on 3/20/25. UT won, 77-62, behind 29 points by Chaz Lanier.
• Wofford is one of four schools, two of which are DI, the Volunteers are 9-0 or better against, alongside Lincoln Memorial (16-0), Emory & Henry (11-0) and Furman (11-0).
• Tennessee owns a 129-18 all-time record versus the current SoCon membership. It has defeated nine of the 11 teams five-plus times.
• Rick Barnes is 33-1 in his career against current SoCon schools, good for his most wins without multiple losses versus any league. He is 18-1 at Tennessee, with the lone setback on 11/11/16.
• Coming off a 19-13 (11-7) campaign, Wofford placed third in the SoCon preseason poll.
• Sophomore guard Chace Watley, a Preseason All-SoCon pick, is the Terriers' top returnee at 9.7 ppg.
 NEWS & NOTES 
• The Volunteers are the only team to play in the Sweet 16 in each of the last four years and in the Elite Eight in each of the past three.
• Last year, Tennessee logged, per CBS, the sixth instance of an SEC team reaching the Sweet 16 at least four years in a row, since the field grew to 32 in 1975.
• UT is, according to Stats Perform, one of three SEC schools—five instances—to make the Elite Eight at least three years in a row, since the tournament expanded to 16 teams in 1951. The others are Kentucky (2010-12, 1995-99, 1956- 58) and Florida (2011-14).
• The Volunteers' +12.6 rebounding margin in 2025-26 was the third-best of the last 30 years (1996- 2026), according to Stats Perform.
• UT had 10-plus offensive boards in 36 of 37 games last year, co-fourth-most in a season the last 30 years (1996-2026), per Stats Perform. Its 44.6 offensive rebounding percentage ranked fourth this century, per KenPom.
• Rick Barnes ' 861 wins are second among active DI coaches and No. 10 all-time (min. 10 years in DI).
• The Volunteers are 36-3 (.923) in Food City Center home openers, with a 33-1 (.971) mark in the last 34 and 10-1 (.909) under Rick Barnes . The average crowd in 38 non-COVID-season home openers is 16,859, with eight over 20,000.
• UT finished 4-1 versus AP top-11 teams, with the wins by 11.3 ppg. It beat #3 Houston (11/25/25) by three, #11 Louisville (12/16/25) by 21, #9 Virginia by seven (3/22/26) and #6 Iowa State by 14 (3/27/26).
• Barnes has led UT to seven of its 10 25-win seasons. The Vols are one of five teams with 25-plus wins in each of the last five years.
• The Vols' 226 wins the last nine seasons (2017-26) rank eighth in DI. Only Houston (273), Gonzaga (270), Duke (255), Kansas (236), Purdue (236), Arizona (230) and Saint Mary's (227) possess more. Liberty (225) and Auburn (224) complete the top 10. In addition, UT is also eighth over the last five seasons (2021-26) with 134 wins.
• UT is the nation's seventh-best program, atop the SEC, the past 10 years (2016-26), per Haslametrics' average end-of-season rankings.
 WINNING WAYS 
• Over the last nine seasons (2017-26), Tennessee (226-85; .724) paces all SEC schools in total victories, overall winning percentage and postseason victories (27). In that span, UT has three SEC titles (2018 and 2024 regular seasons, 2022 tournament).
• In that same period, the Volunteers are one of two SEC teams with even 210-plus wins and/or a winning percentage above .685, alongside Auburn (224-87; .720), which is second in both.
• Over SEC play across the same span, Tennessee (109-52; .677) is first in both league victories and league winning percentage. The only other schools at even 100-plus wins and/or a .620 clip are Kentucky (107-54; .665), Alabama (104-58; .642) and Auburn (103-59; .636).
• In just the last five seasons (2021-26), the Vols own a 134-48 (.736) overall record. That is good for the most total wins and the best winning percentage in the SEC, far ahead of Auburn (.726; 130-49).
• In that time, Tennessee (62-28; .689) is second in league victories and league winning percentage, behind only Alabama (64-26; .711).
 RARE AIR 
•    Tennessee is the lone team to make the Sweet 16 each of the past four years and the Elite Eight each of the last three. 
•    This is only the sixth such occurrence—one other streak was vacated—by any school since the field expanded to 64 teams in 1985.
•    The other instances came from Florida (2011-14), Kansas (2001-04 S16/2002-04 E8), Michigan State (1998-2001 S16/1999-2001 E8), Kentucky (1995-99) and Duke (1986-92 S16/1988-92 E8). Memphis (2006-09 S16/2006-08 E8) had the vacated streak.
•    The Volunteers have also made the Round of 32 in each of the last five years. Only Duke, Kansas and Kentucky from the above list also had a five-year concurrent Round of 32 streak.
 PRESEASON PLAUDITS 
• Juke Harris was tabbed a Preseason Third Team All-American by Blue Ribbon Yearbook. The outlet's only other first-year transfers on the list were Louisville's Flory Bidunga (second team) and St. John's' Tounde Yessoufou (fourth team).
• Harris was one of 20 on the NABC Player of the Year Preseason Watch List. Louisville's Flory Bidunga, Duke's John Blackwell and Kentucky's Milan Momcilovic were the only other first-year transfers.
• The Naismith Trophy Watch List also included Harris as one of 50 selections for the elite group.
• Harris earned Preseason First Team All-SEC status from the media. The lone first-year transfer on the five-man team, he was joined by Rueben Chinyelu, Thomas Haugh, Josh Hubbard and Tyler Tanner.
• The coaches voted Harris a Preseason Second Team All-SEC pick. He was listed with Alex Condon, Milan Momcilovic, Jordan Smith Jr., and Matas Vokietaitis.
• Harris was tabbed to the Julius Erving Award Top 20 Preseason Watch List. He was one of four SEC small forwards who made the cut, alongside Amari Allen, Thomas Haugh and Milan Momcilovic.
 SUPREME SCORERS 
•    Tennessee's nine transfers totaled 3,880 points in 272 appearances last year, good for 14.3 per contest.
•    UT's top seven incoming transfer scorers— Dai Dai Ames , Jalen Haralson , Juke Harris , Terrence Hill Jr. , Braedan Lue , Tyler Lundblade and Miles Rubin — amassed 3,557 points in 232 contests, 15.3 per game.
•    Six of them—all but Lue—led their respective teams in scoring. The top five of that group—Ames, Haralson, Harris, Hill and Lundblade—put up 2,802 points in 164 games, averaging 17.1 per game.
•    Per Basket Under Review's Will Warren, UT is the only team with four transfers who hit 50-plus 3-pointers last year (Ames, Harris, Hill and Lundblade).
 CHICAGO CONNECTION 
•    Tennessee has three players from Chicago, all of whom are in their first year as Volunteers. Dai Dai Ames is a senior who transferred from Cal, Marquis Clark is a freshman and Miles Rubin is a junior who transferred from Loyola Chicago.
•     Amorrow Morgan , who was an assistant coach at Loyola Chicago for two years (2021-23), served as the lead recruiter for all four players. He previously recruited Ames to Cal and Rubin to Loyola Chicago, but did not coach either of them there.
•    Ames and Rubin attended Parker Junior High School together in middle school.
 FORMERLY FOES 
•    Several Tennessee players faced each other in prior seasons. Multiple matchups last year featured strong performances from two future Volunteers.
•    On 3/7/26, Dai Dai Ames scored a career-high 31 points at Wake Forest. Juke Harris had 31 and a career-best 15 rebounds in an 80-73 win  for the Demon Deacons.
•    On 1/30/26, Terrence Hill Jr. , tallied 24 points, six rebounds and five assists in an 89-75 triumph over Loyola Chicago. Miles Rubin finished with 21 points and 10 rebounds for the Ramblers.
•    On 1/2/26, Dai Dai Ames scored  23 points, seven of which came in the final 11 seconds and included a game-winning 4-point play, in a 72-71 home victory over Notre Dame. Jalen Haralson had 17 points, four rebounds and four assists for the Fighting Irish.
•     Jalen Washington played UT thrice last year while at Vanderbilt. He averaged 7.3 ppg, 8.3 rpg and 3.3 bpg. His six blocks on 2/21/26 set a career high.
